text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- PRIVATIZATION OF CELLULAR SERVICES HAS RULES

The Brazilian government on Tuesday took a key step towards the privatization of the country's telecommunications sector when it published bidding rules for concessions to run cellular telephone services.
-- BRETTON WOODS IS OVER, SAYS FRANCO

Central Bank's Foreign Affairs director Gustavo Franco said he is not concerned about Brazil's trade or current account deficit. Franco said worries over the current account deficit is a heritage of 1944 Bretton Woods agreement, which set fixed exchange rates.
-- ITAU NETS 428 MLN REAIS IN NINE MONTHS
Banco Itau had a consolidated net profit of 428 million reais in nine months. Its annual return on equity was 15.8 percent.
-- GE WANTS A BANK IN BRAZIL

Nahid Chicani, General Electric vice-president in Brazil, said the firm's financial arm GE Capital is studying the acquisition of financial institutions in the country. GE Capital has prequalified to participate in the privatization auction of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- FIGHT FOR FUNDS FORCES HEALTH MINISTER TO QUIT

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso accepted the resignation of Health Minister Adib Jatene. His departure began to be negotiated last Wednesday, when Jatene requested an additional 1.6 billion reais for the ministry.
-- NEW TAX FOR SMALL FIRMS
Small firms will be allowed to pay a new single tax of 5.0-7.5 percent beginning Wednesday. The tax will depend on the company's revenues.
-- CELLULAR UNLIKELY TO HAVE AFFECTED FOKKER AIRCRAFT

A federal commission ruled out on Tuesday the possibility that the air disaster involving a TAM Fokker-100 aircraft that killed at least 98 people last week was caused by cellular phones, notebooks or radios.
O GLOBO
-- CONDE FALLS THREE POINTS, SERGIO RISES TWO

An Ibope poll among Rio voters showed Luiz Paulo Conde, the Liberal Front Party (PFL) candidate for Rio de Janeiro mayoral office, lost three points, while his rival Sergio Cabral Filho won two points.
-- PROJECTIONS POINT TO CLINTON'S VICTORY
Democrat President Bill Clinton was projected the winner of the U.S. presidential elections on Tuesday. Clinton will be the first democrat in more than 50 years to be re-elected.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo newsroom, 55-11-2324411
